test_cases.test_case: Add multiple Traveler_Updates then remove all and save modifications
preconditions: Booking detail open for a booking where 'booking_type allows modification' and 'cancellation policy permits modification' (per Booking_Detail_Actions -> Modify preconditions)
User is on the Modify flow
steps: 1. Click the Modify action on the booking detail view
2. Click 'Add Traveler Update' (first time)
3. In Traveler Update entry #1, enter a non-empty update note
4. Click 'Add Traveler Update' (second time)
5. In Traveler Update entry #2, enter a non-empty update note
6. Click 'Add Traveler Update' (third time)
7. In Traveler Update entry #3, enter a non-empty update note
8. For Traveler Update entry #1, click its delete/remove control
9. For Traveler Update entry #2, click its delete/remove control
10. For Traveler Update entry #3, click its delete/remove control (remove all entries)
11. Click Save_Modifications
test_cases.expected_result: Form submits successfully; modifications are applied and Save_Modifications completes without a validation error about missing Traveler_Updates (since Traveler_Updates is not required). A modification confirmation is shown in the UI and a single modification email is sent / visible in the booking activity log (succeeds).

test_cases.test_case: Special_Requests field with a very long string (>200 characters)

test_cases.test_case: Attempt a rapid double-submit of Save_Modifications (idempotency / duplicate-charge guard)
preconditions: Booking detail open for a booking where 'booking_type allows modification' and 'cancellation policy permits modification' (per Booking_Detail_Actions -> Modify preconditions)
User is on the Modify flow and has made a change to Travel_Dates (subject to availability)
steps: 1. Click the Modify action on the booking detail view
2. In Travel_Dates, enter new travel dates (subject to availability)
3. Click Save_Modifications
4. Immediately (within 2 seconds) click Save_Modifications again (before the first save completes)
test_cases.expected_result: The second Save_Modifications attempt is blocked / error shown: the UI displays that the modification is already processing or completed and prevents a duplicate submission. Only one modification is applied; only one modification email appears in the booking activity log and only one fee (if applicable) is charged and shown in the payment summary (is blocked / error shown for duplicate).

test_cases.test_case: Attempt Confirm_Cancellation without opening the cancellation flow (precondition enforcement)

test_cases.test_case: Double-click or rapid repeated click of Book Now on a deal card — second click is blocked to prevent duplicate redirect/promo application

Deals_List is visible with at least one deal card showing a Book_Now button
steps: 1. Locate a deal card in the Deals_List
2. Click the Book_Now button on the deal card
3. Immediately click the Book_Now button again (within one second) on the same deal card
test_cases.expected_result: Second click is blocked; the Book_Now button becomes disabled (or shows a loading state) after the first click and only one redirect to the booking/pre-filled search occurs (no duplicate promo application or multiple redirects are initiated)

test_cases.test_case: Click Logout redirects user to the Home page
preconditions: User logged in as <User>
steps: 1. Navigate to a page where the Logout button is visible
2. Click the Logout button
test_cases.expected_result: Browser is redirected to the Home page; the Home page UI is displayed

test_cases.test_case: After Logout, accessing a protected page redirects to the Login page
preconditions: User logged in as <User>
steps: 1. Navigate to a page where the Logout button is visible
2. Click the Logout button
3. In the same browser session, attempt to navigate to <protected page> (enter the protected page URL or click a bookmark)
test_cases.expected_result: Attempting to access <protected page> redirects to the Login page; the Login page (login form) is displayed

test_cases.test_case: Logout button is not visible when user is not logged in
preconditions: User is not logged in (no active session)
steps: 1. Open a new browser session / incognito window to ensure no authentication state
2. Navigate to the application's main page (where the Logout control would normally appear)
3. Attempt to locate or click the 'Logout' button in the page header or account menu
test_cases.expected_result: The 'Logout' button is not rendered / not visible to the user (no clickable Logout control in header or account menu); the logout action cannot be performed because the precondition (user must be logged in) is not met.

test_cases.test_case: Direct access to logout endpoint while unauthenticated redirects to Login
preconditions: User is not logged in (no active session)
steps: 1. Ensure the browser has no active authenticated session
2. Enter the application's logout endpoint URL (e.g., <Logout endpoint>) directly in the address bar and press Enter
test_cases.expected_result: Browser is redirected to the Login page; the Login form is displayed and no logout operation is performed for any session (there was none). The application blocks the logout action when the precondition 'user must be logged in' is not satisfied.

test_cases.test_case: Access to protected pages is blocked after performing Logout
preconditions: User is logged in as <valid user>
steps: 1. Log in as <valid user>
2. Click the 'Logout' button
3. After being redirected (Logout completes), navigate to a protected page URL (e.g., <protected page>)
test_cases.expected_result: Navigation to <protected page> is blocked: the browser is redirected to the Login page and the protected content is not displayed. The user remains unauthenticated (session terminated and sensitive session data cleared).

test_cases.test_case: Rapid double-click of Logout button
preconditions: user must be logged in
user is on a page showing the 'Logout' button
steps: 1. Click the 'Logout' button once
2. Immediately click the 'Logout' button again (do not wait for redirect to complete)
test_cases.expected_result: First logout action succeeds; the UI redirects to the home page and displays the home page content. The second click is ignored (no additional redirects or error dialogs appear); no protected content is shown and no additional session is created.

test_cases.test_case: Logout in one tab then attempt to use protected page in another tab
preconditions: user must be logged in in two browser tabs (Tab A and Tab B)
both tabs have previously loaded protected pages
steps: 1. In Tab A, click the 'Logout' button
2. Switch to Tab B
3. In Tab B, attempt to access a protected page (e.g., click a saved protected page link or refresh the protected page)
test_cases.expected_result: Logout in Tab A succeeds; Tab A is redirected to the home page. In Tab B, the attempt to access the protected page is blocked; the UI redirects Tab B to the login page and protected content is not displayed.

test_cases.test_case: Use browser Back button after logout to return to protected page
preconditions: user must be logged in and currently viewing a protected page
the browser history contains the protected page and previous pages
steps: 1. Click the 'Logout' button
2. After the UI redirects to the home page, press the browser Back button once to try to return to the protected page
test_cases.expected_result: Logout succeeds; the UI is on the home page. Using the Back button to return to the protected page is blocked; the application redirects the user to the login page and the protected content is not shown.
